page: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processors operating at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 104 physical cores and 208 vCPUs via hyperthreading, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 5700.0 GB, translating to 27.4 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server includes a bundled 8389 GB SSD, and it supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the moderate 2.7 GHz clock speed of the Intel Xeon architecture. However, the massive core count enables top-tier multi-core performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks, all ranking in the top 10%. Memory performance is exceptionally strong, with read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks consistently reaching top-tier status. Redis SET operations also achieve top-tier throughput, registering 162.62 million operations per second.

Given the massive memory footprint and high core count, this server represents a high-density resource profile. The qualitative cost efficiency is optimized for workloads that require massive datasets to reside entirely in memory, reducing the need for distributed clustering. The combination of 5.7 TB of RAM, a large local SSD, and high multi-core throughput makes this instance recommended for large-scale relational databases, in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise SAP HANA deployments, and heavy data warehousing. It is less effective for single-threaded tasks or workloads requiring GPU acceleration.
